items.stem: Why must a network call in Android use a coroutine or background dispatcher rather than running directly on the main thread?

options.text: The main thread handles UI; blocking it freezes the app and can trigger an ANR
options.rationale: Correct: long work on the main thread blocks rendering and input, causing Application Not Responding.

options.text: The main thread cannot execute Kotlin functions
options.rationale: It runs Kotlin code; the issue is blocking it, not capability.
They provide concurrency and cancellation, not raw speed.

options.text: Android forbids all I/O in Kotlin
options.rationale: I/O is allowed; it must just happen off the main thread.

items.explanation: Correct: long work on the main thread blocks rendering and input, causing Application Not Responding.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about Kotlin null safety? (Select TWO)

options.text: A type must be declared nullable with ? to hold null
options.rationale: Correct: non-null types cannot hold null unless marked with ?.

options.text: The safe-call operator ?. returns null instead of throwing when the receiver is null
options.rationale: Correct: ?. short-circuits to null on a null receiver.

options.text: The !! operator makes a value safe to use
options.rationale: !! asserts non-null and throws if the value is null; it is not safe.

options.text: All Kotlin types are nullable by default
options.rationale: Types are non-null by default; nullability is opt-in.

items.explanation: Correct: non-null types cannot hold null unless marked with ?.

items.stem: What is the main reason to keep screen state in a ViewModel rather than in a composable?

options.text: The ViewModel survives configuration changes like rotation
options.rationale: Correct: a ViewModel outlives recomposition and recreation, so state is not lost on rotation.
They can via remember, but that state is tied to composition lifetime.
ViewModels do not render UI at all.
Both require Kotlin; this is about state lifetime.

items.explanation: Correct: a ViewModel outlives recomposition and recreation, so state is not lost on rotation.
